storyParas: This map shows the world boundary in the years Marco Polo was alive. The borders show different kingdoms/countries at that time.

There is a checkbox in top left corner to see the location in current world map.
Born in 1254, in Venice (present Italy).
Studied commercial arithmetic, Latin literacy, and the lingua franca of the eastern Mediterranean.
In 1269, his father and uncle returned from Mongol, carrying letters from Kublai Khan.
After 2 years from here, aged 17, Marco Polo along with his father and uncle would start his expedition to Mongols.

In the year, 1271, he starts the long expedition and reaches Acre & Jerusalem and stops to collect holy oil from the Holy Sepulchre on instructions from the Pope. They were instructed by pope to do this.
After travelling for a year, in the year 1272, they reach and travel through the mountains of Armenia and eastern Anatolia. Modern day  Erzurum, Turkey.
In same year 1272, Marco Polo crossed through Persian town called Toris
He described it as grand city and a spectacular commercial hub having excellent geographic position attracted traders from India, Baghdad, Mosul, and Europe.
He observed that the local inhabitants made their living entirely through trade and manufacturing crafts.
Religious demographic : large population of Muslims alongside various Eastern Christian sects, including Nestorians, Armenians, and Jacobites.
In the year 1273, Polos reached Gormuz (Iran) planning to buy ship and sail from here.
He noted that during the peak summer months, the heat was so intense that locals were forced to leave the city and sleep in cabins built over the water or submerged in rivers to survive.
Seeing the ships condition, without any iron nails, just tied together by coconut waste, Polos decided to take land route
Rest of the 1273 AD was passed while crossing Afghanistan mountaneous deserts and passes.
He saw ancient marble palaces and grand ruins that showed past wealth in present day Balkh, Afghanistan.
Then he crossed Afghanistan-Tajikistan border and Marco Polo wrote about the bitter cold and thin air of the place.
Wrote about large wild sheep with huge horns—now known as Marco Polo sheep—roaming the high, lonely plateaus.
